collection_summary:
Original `comparative` instance filling one of the remaining gap-4 categories (comparative: 0 reg + 1 staged → 2 staged after this instance). NEW **Sports/Tennis** subdomain in Sports family (joins Olympic host cities; second Sports-family instance). NEW entity class: tennis players — the first athlete-keyed instance in pkdb_bench (existing Sports/Olympics instance is host-city-keyed, not athlete-keyed). Proves the comparative primitive beyond country-keyed entities (the existing `countries_with_more_than_5_fields_medalists` is country-keyed; this instance uses the same '>5' comparator on athletes).

Natural human query: 'Which tennis players have won more than five Grand Slam singles titles in the Open Era, and how many has each player won — separately for the men's and women's tour?'

Multi-wiki source plan (4 URLs): 2 master Grand Slam championship articles (men's + women's) supply the universe (all Open Era singles champions) and per-player title counts via tournament-level tabulation; 2 Open Era records pages aggregate per-player Open Era totals (useful for cross-validation, especially for split-career players whose totals differ from lifetime totals). Master articles are the universe-defining source; Open Era records pages cross-validate per-player counts.

Result: 119 rows × 5 columns (Player PK + Grand Slam Singles Titles numeric + Tour categorical + Nationality categorical + Qualifies (>5) boolean), single-key PK on Player, 0 duplicates. Tour distribution: 58 Men's, 61 Women's. 24 of 119 players qualify (>5 strict): 13 men (Djokovic 24, Nadal 22, Federer 20, Sampras 14, Borg 11, Connors 8, Lendl 8, Agassi 8, McEnroe 7, Wilander 7, Alcaraz 7, Edberg 6, Becker 6) + 11 women (Serena 23, Graf 22, Evert 18, Navratilova 18, Court 11, Seles 9, King 8, Goolagong Cawley 7, Henin 7, Venus 7, Świątek 6). Title range: 1 (many players) to 24 (Djokovic). Two players at exactly 5 (Sharapova, Hingis) → Qualifies=FALSE under strict '>5' rule.

Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles + deserts-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Player (Wikipedia article-title name); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 master + 2 records articles; (c) Open Era cutoff '1968 onwards strict' (Margaret Court 11 of 24 lifetime; King 8 of 12 lifetime; Laver 5 of 11; Rosewall 4 of 8; Newcombe 5 of 7); (d) deterministic Nationality rule for split-career players (flag-grounded majority-of-wins per master tournament-listing flags + Open Era records pages, with chronologically-first as tiebreaker for 1-1 splits like Kriek); (e) explicit comparator semantics ('more than 5' strict = ≥6; Sharapova and Hingis at exactly 5 are FALSE); (f) source-defined universe (all Open Era Grand Slam singles champions per master articles, no curator selection within universe).
source_coverage_notes:
Four Wikipedia source URLs combine. The 2 master tournament-listing articles define the universe (all Open Era Grand Slam singles champions) and provide tournament-level per-event title cells, from which per-player counts are aggregated. The 2 Open Era records pages aggregate per-player Open Era totals and serve as cross-validation for the counts derived from the master tournament listings.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Grand_Slam_men%27s_singles_champions): universe + value. Tabulates every men's Grand Slam singles champion by year × tournament from 1877 onwards. Filtered to Open Era (1968 onwards), this defines the 58 unique men's universe and gives per-event title attribution.
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Grand_Slam_women%27s_singles_champions): universe + value. Same pattern for women's, defining the 61 unique women's universe.
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Era_tennis_records_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_singles): ranking + cross-validation. Aggregates per-player Open Era singles title totals for men, used to cross-validate counts derived from the master tournament listings. Confirms Djokovic 24, Nadal 22, Federer 20, Sampras 14, Borg 11, Connors 8, Lendl 8, Agassi 8, McEnroe 7, Wilander 7, Alcaraz 7, Edberg 6, Becker 6 as the 13 men's qualifiers (>5).
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Era_tennis_records_%E2%80%93_Women%27s_singles): ranking + cross-validation. Same pattern for women's. Confirms Serena 23, Graf 22, Evert 18, Navratilova 18, Court 11, Seles 9, King 8, Goolagong Cawley 7, Henin 7, Venus 7, Świątek 6 as the 11 women's qualifiers (>5).

Validation note: per-player Open Era title counts in the staged data are sourced from cross-referencing the 2 master Grand Slam articles (tournament-level) with the 2 Open Era records pages (player-level aggregation). For split-career players (Court, King, Laver, Rosewall, Newcombe), the staged count is the Open Era subset of their lifetime total (counted from 1968 French Open onwards, the first Open Era major).

Nationality provenance (cycle-2 audit S1 clarification + cycle-4 sub-tiebreaker addition): Nationality is derived from the country flags shown in the 2 master tournament-listing articles next to each player's title-winning entry, combined with the country flags shown next to each player's row in the 2 Open Era records pages. For split-career players whose flags differ across their titles (Lendl, Seles, Navratilova, Kriek, Rybakina, Graf, Becker), the staged Nationality is the country represented in the majority of the player's Open Era title-winning matches (majority-of-wins rule). For 1-1 flag splits with no majority (Kriek: 1981 AO South African + 1982 AO US), a chronologically-first sub-tiebreaker resolves to the earlier title's flag (Kriek → South African). For successor-state cases (Graf/Becker: West Germany 1985-1989 → reunified Germany 1990+), the staged value normalizes to the post-reunification successor state ('German'). The 4 cited source URLs are sufficient to recover Nationality for all 119 players without separate per-player Wikipedia articles, because the flag-per-title cells in the master listings are the canonical title-winning representation record.

Universe-size sanity: 119 staged rows = 58 men's + 61 women's Open Era Grand Slam singles champions. The 2 master tournament articles list every singles champion 1877-present; filtering to Open Era (1968 onwards) gives the staged universe. Title distribution (full universe, sorted DESC by titles, regenerated from CSV in cycle-2): 1 player at 24 (Djokovic), 1 at 23 (Serena), 2 at 22 (Nadal, Graf), 1 at 20 (Federer), 2 at 18 (Evert, Navratilova), 1 at 14 (Sampras), 2 at 11 (Borg, Court), 1 at 9 (Seles), 4 at 8 (Agassi, Connors, King, Lendl), 6 at 7 (Alcaraz, Goolagong Cawley, Henin, McEnroe, Venus, Wilander), 3 at 6 (Becker, Edberg, Świątek), 4 at 5 (Hingis, Laver, Newcombe, Sharapova), 9 at 4 (Sinner, Courier, Vilas, Rosewall on men's; Osaka, Sabalenka, Clijsters, Sánchez Vicario, Mandlíková on women's), 10 at 3 (Kuerten, Ashe, Kodeš, Murray, Wawrinka on men's; Davenport, Capriati, Barty, Kerber, Wade on women's), 20 at 2 (Bruguera, Rafter, Hewitt, Safin, Kriek, Smith, Năstase, Kafelnikov on men's; Pierce, Austin, Kvitová, Mauresmo, Kuznetsova, Muguruza, Halep, Gauff, Azarenka, Li Na, Krejčíková, Rybakina on women's), 52 at 1 (long tail of 26 men's + 26 women's one-major champions). Total: 1+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+4+6+3+4+9+10+20+52 = 119. The single-title tail dominates the universe by row count (~44%).

Comparator distribution: 24 of 119 players qualify (>5 strict, ≥6). Non-qualifiers include Sharapova and Hingis at exactly 5 titles each (FALSE under strict '>5' = '≥6'). Per-tour qualifier rate: 13 of 58 men (22%); 11 of 61 women (18%). Universe is heavily skewed toward one-major winners (long tail), which is the comparator's challenge — most players are NOT qualifiers but the model must compute counts and apply the comparator correctly across all 119.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with three documented risks resolved at staging. R1: pre-Open-Era amateur titles muddy the universe and per-player counts (Margaret Court 24 lifetime vs 11 Open Era; Billie Jean King 12 vs 8; Laver/Rosewall/Newcombe spanning the 1968 transition) — committed to Open Era only (1968 onwards strict) with explicit per-player Open Era counts for the 5 cross-era players. R2: nationality is contested for split-career players (Lendl, Navratilova, Seles, Kriek, Rybakina, Graf/Becker pre-/post-reunification) — committed to flag-grounded 'nationality per the country flag in the master tournament-listing articles (cross-validated by Open Era records pages)', with majority-of-wins as the primary tiebreaker and chronologically-first as a sub-tiebreaker for 1-1 splits (Kriek); 6 flagged in normalization_decisions. R3: comparator '>5' is strict (≥6); Sharapova and Hingis at exactly 5 titles each are FALSE — committed to strict '>5' semantics and documented in the boolean column header.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses tennis players. Closest in shape is the existing comparative instance `countries_with_more_than_5_fields_medalists` — same '>5' comparator pattern but with countries-as-entities; tennis players prove the primitive on athletes-as-entities.
- Category: comparative (primary, '>5 Grand Slam singles titles' boolean comparator across all players). Secondary: aggregation (counting Open Era titles per player from tournament-level master tables).
- Source plan: 4 Wikipedia URLs (2 master tournament-listing articles + 2 Open Era records aggregation articles). Master articles define universe + tournament-level data; records articles aggregate per-player totals for cross-validation.
- Expected shape: 119 rows × 5 cols, single PK on Player.
- Domain: Sports/Tennis — NEW subdomain in Sports family (joins Sports/Olympics from `summer_olympics_hosts_1960_2020`).
- Entity-class diversity (encouragement): tennis players is the FIRST athlete-keyed instance in pkdb_bench (Olympic instance is host-city-keyed). Strong application of the entity-class-diversity encouragement from instance_selection_priorities.md.
- Risks/adaptation: per the three pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) title counts are temporally-sensitive for active players (Djokovic, Alcaraz, Sinner, Świątek, Sabalenka, Gauff may increment); temporal_sensitivity = medium reflects this; (b) row count 119 is on the higher end of recent staged-instance band (12-25 typical, 60-285 for larger universes like cities/SCOTUS/Nobel works) — universe-heavy comparative pattern is the design intent and matches the Fields-medalists shape with a denser universe; (c) name normalization for diacritics (Björn Borg, Andrés Gimeno, Goran Ivanišević, Jeļena Ostapenko, Marin Čilić) — committed to Wikipedia article-title diacritic forms.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Open Era cutoff: '1968 onwards strict'. The 1968 French Open was the first Open Era major; Open Era titles begin with the 1968 French Open onwards. Titles won at any tournament before that (including the January 1968 Australian Open) are excluded. For cross-era players: Margaret Court 11 (1969 AO/FO/US; 1970 all four; 1971 AO; 1973 AO/FO/US); Billie Jean King 8 (Wim 1968 [July, first Open Era Wimbledon], US 1971/1972/1974, Wim 1972/1973/1975, FO 1972 — her January 1968 AO win was pre-Open and is excluded); Rod Laver 5 (1968 Wim, 1969 calendar slam = AO/FO/Wim/US); Ken Rosewall 4 (FO 1968, US 1970, AO 1971/1972); John Newcombe 5 (Wim 1970/1971, US 1973, AO 1973/1975). Excluded entirely (pre-Open-Era career only): Maria Bueno (7 lifetime, all pre-1968).
2) Comparator '>5' strict: 'more than 5' is strictly > 5 (i.e., ≥ 6). Sharapova at exactly 5 and Hingis at exactly 5 are FALSE. Documented in column-header form 'Qualifies (>5)' for unambiguity.
3) Nationality rule: nationality at title-winning per the country flag shown in the master tournament-listing articles (and the country flag in the Open Era records pages for split-career players); majority-of-wins as tiebreaker. The 4 cited source URLs are sufficient to recover Nationality for all 119 players via the flag-per-title cells — no per-player Wikipedia articles needed. For split-career players: Lendl 'Czechoslovak' (all 8 titles 1984-1990 with Czechoslovak flag before US naturalization 1992); Navratilova 'American' (all 18 titles 1978+ with US flag; defected 1975); Seles 'Yugoslav' (8 of 9 titles 1990-1993 with Yugoslav flag pre-US-naturalization 1994; majority-of-wins); Kriek 'South African' (1-1 split between 1981 AO with South African flag and 1982 AO with US flag; chronologically-first tiebreaker for 1-1 flag splits resolves to 1981 SA); Rybakina 'Kazakhstani' (both Open Era titles 2022 Wim + 2026 AO with Kazakhstan flag after 2018 federation switch); Graf 'German' and Becker 'German' (the master listings show a West German flag for their pre-1990 titles and a German flag for their 1990+ titles; both are normalized to a single 'German' Nationality value under the schema's flag-normalization rule treating the post-reunification successor state as the canonical form).
4) Tour values: 'Men's' and 'Women's' (two values only). Apostrophe-S form per standard tennis nomenclature. No 'Mixed' or other values (singles only by design).
5) Title counts current as of access date: both tours through 2026 Australian Open — the most recent completed Grand Slam tournament. Alcaraz 7 (men's) and Rybakina 2 (women's) reflect their 2026 AO wins. Active players may increment after subsequent tournaments. temporal_sensitivity = medium.
6) Sort order: Grand Slam Singles Titles DESC primary, Player ASC tiebreaker. Cross-tour (men and women interleave at same title count). Natural for the comparative 'most prolific Grand Slam champions' framing.
7) Boolean encoding: 'true' / 'false' (lowercase strings in CSV) for the Qualifies (>5) column.
8) operation_type 'aggregation' chosen — per-player title count is a GROUP BY aggregation over the tournament-level master tables. Comparator predicate (>5) is layered on the aggregation result.
9) claim_type 'source_defined' — universe is defined by the master tournament-listing articles filtered to Open Era. No curator selection within universe; all Open Era Grand Slam singles champions are included.
10) Name normalization: Wikipedia article-title forms with full diacritics preserved (Björn Borg, Goran Ivanišević, Iga Świątek, Marin Čilić, Jeļena Ostapenko). Hyphenated/multi-part surnames per article title (Evonne Goolagong Cawley, Arantxa Sánchez Vicario, Juan Martín del Potro, Coco Gauff). For Carlos Alcaraz (article title 'Carlos Alcaraz Garfia' redirected from 'Carlos Alcaraz'), use the redirected common-form 'Carlos Alcaraz'.
normalization_decisions: Player (PK) values use Wikipedia article-title common-name forms with full diacritics preserved ('Björn Borg', 'Iga Świątek', 'Goran Ivanišević', 'Marin Čilić', 'Jeļena Ostapenko'). Hyphenated/multi-part surnames follow article title forms ('Evonne Goolagong Cawley', 'Arantxa Sánchez Vicario', 'Juan Martín del Potro', 'Coco Gauff'). For 'Carlos Alcaraz' the short common form (rather than 'Carlos Alcaraz Garfia') is used. Grand Slam Singles Titles is numeric integer; Open Era only (titles from 1968 French Open onwards). For cross-era players, only Open Era subset is counted (Court 11, King 8, Laver 5, Rosewall 4, Newcombe 5). Tour values use two-valued enum: 'Men's' / 'Women's' (apostrophe-S form). Nationality is a single-valued categorical using common-form English adjectival nationality names derived from the country flag in the master tournament-listing articles (cross-validated by Open Era records pages), e.g., 'American', 'Swiss', 'Czechoslovak', 'German', 'Australian'. For split-career players, the nationality at title-winning per majority-of-wins is staged, grounded in the country flag shown in the master tournament listings and Open Era records pages (no per-player Wikipedia articles needed): Lendl 'Czechoslovak' (all 8 titles pre-1992 naturalization, Czechoslovak flag in master); Seles 'Yugoslav' (8 of 9 pre-1994 naturalization, Yugoslav flag in master); Navratilova 'American' (all titles 1978+ as US-resident, US flag in master); Kriek 'South African' (1-1 split 1981 SA / 1982 US; chronologically-first tiebreaker); Rybakina 'Kazakhstani' (both Open Era titles 2022 Wim + 2026 AO with Kazakhstan flag after 2018 federation switch); Graf and Becker 'German' (West-German-flag titles before 1990 and German-flag titles 1990+ are normalized to a single 'German' Nationality value, treating the post-reunification successor state as the canonical form). Qualifies (>5) is boolean with strict 'more than 5' semantics (>5 = ≥6); values are lowercase string 'true' / 'false' for CSV-cleanliness. Two players at exactly 5 titles (Sharapova, Hingis) are FALSE under this rule. Sort order: Grand Slam Singles Titles DESC primary, Player ASC tiebreaker.
open_questions: 1) Open Era cutoff scope: staged values count only Open Era titles for cross-era players. An LLM under test reporting lifetime totals (Court 24, King 12, Laver 11) instead of Open Era totals (Court 11, King 8, Laver 5) could be partially credited as defensible alternative reading. 2) Comparator strictness: '>5' is strict (≥6). An LLM treating it as ≥5 would incorrectly flag Sharapova and Hingis as qualifiers (5 each). 3) Nationality rule for split-career players: staged 'nationality at title-winning per flag-grounded majority-of-wins; chronologically-first sub-tiebreaker for 1-1 flag splits (Kriek); post-reunification successor state for West Germany→Germany (Graf, Becker)'. Alternative readings: 'current nationality' (would give Lendl American, Seles American); 'birth nationality' (would give Navratilova Czechoslovak, Rybakina Russian); 'latest-flag tiebreaker for 1-1 splits' (would give Kriek American). 6 players flagged: Lendl, Seles, Navratilova, Kriek, Rybakina, Graf/Becker. 4) Title-count freshness: counts current through 2026 AO for both tours. Active players (Djokovic, Alcaraz, Sinner, Świątek, Sabalenka, Gauff, etc.) may increment. An LLM with a later cutoff could legitimately report higher counts. 5) Universe scope: Open Era Grand Slam singles only. Doubles, mixed doubles, junior, wheelchair, year-end championships are excluded. An LLM including any of these would over-count. 6) Tour values: 'Men's' / 'Women's' two-valued enum. No nonbinary, mixed, or other Tour categories (singles-only by design). 7) Name normalization: Wikipedia article-title common-name forms. An LLM using alternative forms (e.g., 'Goolagong' alone instead of 'Evonne Goolagong Cawley'; 'Bjorn Borg' without diacritic) could be partially credited as defensible. 8) Carlos Alcaraz 7 titles: his 2026 AO win brings him to 7 as of source-access date; older snapshots may show 6 or fewer. 9) Counts for several recent first-time champions (Madison Keys 2025 AO, Markéta Vondroušová 2023 Wim, Coco Gauff 2023 US Open + 2025 FO = 2) — current as of source-access date. 10) Margaret Court is sometimes cited with 24 'Grand Slam' titles in popular sources without distinguishing Open Era vs amateur; staged value 11 explicitly reflects the Open Era-only rule and may differ from popular-source recollection.

cycle_1.summary: Cycle-1 was the audit pass on the initial-stage artifact. Auditor flagged 3 BLOCKING findings (women's universe + counts incomplete, temporal cutoff inconsistent, Vondroušová diacritic violation) plus 1 hygiene + 1 suggestion. See cycle_2 for repair details.

cycle_2.verdict: Repair pass — addressing cycle-1 audit findings
blocking_addressed: B1 (factual + structural, BLOCKING — women's universe incomplete + count errors): cycle-1 staging missed Victoria Azarenka entirely (she has 2 Open Era titles: 2012 AO, 2013 AO, Belarusian) and undercounted three women's players by 1 each: Li Na 1 → 2 (cycle-1 missed her 2014 AO; correct count is 2011 FO + 2014 AO); Barbora Krejčíková 1 → 2 (cycle-1 missed her 2024 Wimbledon; correct count is 2021 FO + 2024 Wimbledon); Elena Rybakina 1 → 2 (under the corrected 2026 AO temporal cutoff, her 2022 Wim + 2026 AO win = 2 titles). Cycle-2 fix: added Azarenka row (Tour Women's, Titles 2, Nationality Belarusian, Qualifies false); updated Li Na/Krejčíková/Rybakina title counts 1 → 2. Universe size 118 → 119 unique players; women's count 60 → 61 women; qualifier count unchanged at 24 (no count change pushed anyone past the >5 threshold). Sort order automatically rebalanced via re-sort by Titles DESC then Player ASC.

B2 (factual + structural, BLOCKING — temporal cutoff inconsistent across tours): cycle-1 staging used '2026 Australian Open' for men's title counts but '2025 US Open' for women's, even though the cited women's master article ('List of Grand Slam women's singles champions') already tabulates 2026 AO results. Cycle-2 fix: aligned both tours to '2026 Australian Open' cutoff — the most recent completed Grand Slam tournament as of the 2026-05-12 source-access date. Rybakina 2026 AO win reflected (B1 fold-in). Updated narrative in temporal_note (draft.json), _extraction_notes (draft.json), and decision_log Rule 5 (curation.json) to state both tours consistently through 2026 AO.

B3 (structural, BLOCKING — Vondroušová diacritic rule violation): cycle-1 staging used 'Marketa Vondrousova' (no diacritics), violating the declared rule 'Wikipedia article-title common-name forms with full diacritics preserved' (per normalization_decisions Rule 10). The Wikipedia article title is 'Markéta Vondroušová' (with é and ová diacritics). Cycle-2 fix: renamed CSV row 'Marketa Vondrousova' → 'Markéta Vondroušová' to honor the article-title-with-diacritics rule. No other diacritic violations found on spot-check (Björn Borg, Goran Ivanišević, Iga Świątek, Marin Čilić, Jeļena Ostapenko, Andrés Gimeno, Andrés Gómez, Hana Mandlíková, Petra Kvitová, Barbora Krejčíková, Conchita Martínez, Carlos Moyá, Juan Martín del Potro, Arantxa Sánchez Vicario, Ilie Năstase all already in full-diacritic form).
hygiene_addressed: H1 (structural, HYGIENE — title-bucket distribution narrative inconsistent with CSV): cycle-1 source_coverage_notes narrative said '8 at 4, 13 at 3, 14 at 2' but the actual staged-CSV distribution was '9 at 4, 10 at 3, 16 at 2' (cycle-1 hand-counted prose drifted from the data). After B1 row additions/corrections, the correct cycle-2 distribution is: 1+1+2+1+2+1+2+1+4+6+3+4+9+10+20+52 = 119 (sum verified). Cycle-2 fix: regenerated the title-bucket distribution sentence in source_coverage_notes from the cycle-2 CSV (4 at 5 now includes Laver and Newcombe at 5 alongside Sharapova and Hingis — cycle-1 prose had missed the men's-side 5-title players; 20 at 2 now includes Azarenka/Li Na/Krejčíková/Rybakina as added/corrected by B1).
suggestion_addressed: S1 (structural, SUGGESTION — Nationality provenance under-specified): cycle-1 narrative invoked 'Wikipedia article foregrounding' for split-career player nationality, but per-player Wikipedia articles are not in source_urls (only 2 master tournament articles + 2 Open Era records pages = 4 sources). Cycle-2 fix: clarified Nationality provenance in source_coverage_notes — Nationality is derived from the country flags in the master tournament-listing articles (per-title cells) combined with the per-player flags in the Open Era records pages, applying majority-of-wins for split-career players. The 4 cited source URLs are sufficient to recover Nationality for all 119 players; no per-player articles needed. The 6 split-career edge cases (Lendl, Seles, Navratilova, Kriek, Rybakina, Graf/Becker) are all flag-grounded in the 4 cited sources via their per-title flag attribution.

cycle_3.verdict: Repair pass — addressing cycle-2 audit findings (1 BLOCKING + 4 HYGIENE)
blocking_addressed: B1 (structural, BLOCKING — db_analog Open Era predicate would include pre-Open-Era 1968 AO): cycle-1 db_analog used `WHERE t.tournament_date >= '1968-01-01'`, which is logically inconsistent with the staged data — the 1968 Australian Open was held in January 1968 and was an amateur-era event (won by Bill Bowrey). Including it in the SQL would add Bowrey as a phantom champion and overcount Billie Jean King by 1 (her 1968 AO is amateur-era). Cycle-3 fix: changed the predicate to `WHERE t.is_open_era = TRUE` — a semantic flag that correctly excludes the 1968 AO regardless of date-arithmetic edge cases. The Open Era started at the 1968 French Open (late May 1968), not the 1968 AO; the staged CSV correctly reflects this (Bowrey absent; King at 8 not 9; Court at 11 not adjusted). The semantic flag is preferred over a date-cutoff like `>= '1968-05-27'` because it stays correct even if specific tournament dates are interpreted differently across sources.
hygiene_addressed: H1 (factual + structural, HYGIENE — stale 118 row-count residues in active narrative): cycle-2 universe size update (118 → 119) did not fully propagate to all active narrative locations. Cycle-3 fix: corrected source_coverage_notes Comparator distribution sentence '24 of 118 players' → '24 of 119 players'; corrected decision_log Pre-gate 'Expected shape: ~118 rows' → '119 rows'; corrected decision_log risk (b) 'row count 118 is on the higher end' → 'row count 119 is on the higher end'. Cycle-2 had updated collection_summary, _extraction_notes, source_coverage_notes universe-size sanity, and the title distribution sum, but missed these 3 stale 118 references.

H2 (factual + scope, HYGIENE — stale 2025 US Open women cutoff in open_questions): cycle-2 fixed the temporal cutoff in temporal_note, _extraction_notes, and decision_log Rule 5 to '2026 Australian Open for both tours', but open_questions item 4 still said 'counts current through 2026 AO (men) and 2025 US Open (women)'. Cycle-3 fix: corrected open_questions item 4 to 'counts current through 2026 AO for both tours' for consistency with the cycle-2 cutoff alignment.

H3 (structural, HYGIENE — Rybakina 'only title' prose stale after cycle-2 count update): cycle-2 updated Rybakina's CSV row to 2 titles, but the prose narrative in temporal_note, decision_log Rule 3, and normalization_decisions still described her as having 'only her 2022 Wimbledon title' / 'her only title 2022'. Cycle-3 fix: updated all three narrative locations to say 'both Open Era titles 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 Australian Open with Kazakhstan flag' to match the cycle-2 CSV correction.

H4 (structural, HYGIENE — flag-grounded nationality provenance not propagated): cycle-2 added the Nationality provenance clarification (master-table country flags + Open Era records page flags, majority-of-wins) only to source_coverage_notes, but the related Nationality discussions in decision_log Rule 3 and normalization_decisions still invoked the older 'Wikipedia article foregrounding' framing. Cycle-3 fix: rewrote decision_log Rule 3 and normalization_decisions to lead with the flag-grounded provenance ('country flag in master tournament listings + Open Era records pages, majority-of-wins as tiebreaker') and explicitly state that the 4 cited URLs are sufficient — no per-player articles needed. Same wording across all three narrative locations now.

H5 (structural, HYGIENE — stale ASCII 'Marketa Vondrousova' in open_questions): cycle-2 fixed the CSV row to 'Markéta Vondroušová' but the open_questions item 9 still spelled her name as 'Marketa Vondrousova' (ASCII, no diacritics) when describing her as a recent first-time champion. Cycle-3 fix: corrected open_questions item 9 to use the full-diacritic 'Markéta Vondroušová' form, matching the CSV and the declared name-normalization rule.

cycle_4.verdict: Repair pass — addressing cycle-3 audit findings (1 BLOCKING + 3 HYGIENE, ~5 minimal fixes)
blocking_addressed: B1 (factual, BLOCKING — Kriek 1-1 flag split not derivable under declared rule): Cycle-3 staged Kriek as 'American' citing 'article foregrounding' as the tiebreaker, but article foregrounding was no longer part of the declared rule after the cycle-3 flag-grounded propagation. Kriek's flag split is 1-1: 1981 AO with South African flag, 1982 AO with US flag. Majority-of-wins gives no winner. Cycle-4 fix: (a) introduced an explicit sub-tiebreaker rule for 1-1 flag splits — 'chronologically-first Open Era title flag wins' — documented in decision_log Rule 3 and normalization_decisions; (b) under this rule, Kriek 1981 AO South African flag wins; CSV row changed 'Johan Kriek,2,Men's,American,false' → 'Johan Kriek,2,Men's,South African,false'; (c) propagated 'South African' across all narrative locations (temporal_note, decision_log Rule 3, normalization_decisions). The chronologically-first sub-tiebreaker is preferred over 'most-recent-flag' because it is deterministic, source-defensible from the master listings, and applies symmetrically across any 1-1 tie that might emerge in future updates.

H4 (factual, HYGIENE — Billie Jean King's pre-Open 1968 AO incorrectly included in the Open Era 8-title breakdown): cycle-1 decision_log Rule 1 listed King's 8 Open Era titles as 'AO 1968, FO 1972, Wim 1968/1972/1973/1975, US 1971/1972/1974' — that is 9 items, with the AO 1968 (January 1968, pre-Open Era under our 1968 French Open start cutoff) erroneously counted. King's correct 8 Open Era titles: Wim 1968 (July, first Open Era Wimbledon), FO 1972, Wim 1972, Wim 1973, Wim 1975, US 1971, US 1972, US 1974. Cycle-4 fix: removed AO 1968 from decision_log Rule 1; added an explicit clarifying note that the January 1968 AO win was pre-Open and is excluded.

hygiene_addressed: H1 (structural, HYGIENE — chronologically-first sub-tiebreaker not propagated to source_coverage_notes or open_questions): cycle-4 documented the 1-1 sub-tiebreaker in decision_log Rule 3 and normalization_decisions but did not propagate it to source_coverage_notes Nationality-provenance paragraph or open_questions item 3 Nationality discussion. Cycle-6 fix: added the chronologically-first sub-tiebreaker mention to source_coverage_notes Nationality-provenance paragraph (with Kriek as the worked example) and expanded open_questions item 3 to enumerate the 1-1-split sub-tiebreaker and the successor-state Graf/Becker rule as alternative-reading flags for the model under test.

H2 (factual, HYGIENE — Graf/Becker 'Wikipedia foregrounds' invokes article framing instead of flag normalization): cycle-3 propagated flag-grounded framing for most split-career players but the Graf/Becker line in normalization_decisions (and a similar phrasing in decision_log Rule 3) still said 'Wikipedia foregrounds German', which appeals to article framing rather than the declared flag-grounded rule. Cycle-6 fix: rewrote the Graf/Becker line in 3 active locations (temporal_note, decision_log Rule 3, normalization_decisions) to use flag-normalization framing — 'West-German-flag titles before 1990 and German-flag titles 1990+ are normalized to a single German value under the schema's flag-normalization rule treating the post-reunification successor state as the canonical form'. The successor-state rule is now an explicit named sub-rule alongside chronologically-first.

H3 (structural, HYGIENE — 'April 1968 French Open' wording was imprecise): cycle-1 temporal_note said the Open Era cutoff is 'April 1968 French Open being the first Open Era major' but the 1968 French Open was actually held in late May–early June 1968 (the 'April 1968' wording likely conflated the Open Era political decision in April 1968 with the tournament date). Cycle-1 decision_log Rule 1 also said 'titles won before April 1968 are excluded', which is technically correct but imprecise — the January 1968 AO is the only pre-Open major in 1968 itself. Cycle-6 fix: rewrote temporal_note to say 'the 1968 French Open being the first Open Era major' (drop the misleading 'April'); rewrote decision_log Rule 1 to say 'Open Era titles begin with the 1968 French Open onwards; titles won at any tournament before that (including the January 1968 Australian Open) are excluded' — more precise and avoids the date-of-decision-vs-date-of-tournament confusion.
